# BCG Calculator

IMPORTANT NOTE: if you are using the BCG results, your data should be
collected and processed using these field and laboratory protocols
[<a href="https://github.com/Blocktt/LowerBoiseBCGCalc/blob/main/inst/apps/LowerBoiseBCGCalc/www/links/Methods_Bugs_Fish_20260525.pdf" target="_blank">PDF</a>].

-   Macroinvertebrates: USGS National Water‑Quality Assessment (NAWQA)
    Richest Targeted Habitat (RTH) method

-   Fish: composite of two electrofishing passes - one through
    deep-water areas with a boat or tow barge; the second through
    shallower riffle areas with a backpack electrofisher

[**STEP 1: Go to the 'Import File' tab and upload the File Builder
output file**]{.underline}

(Should be named BCG_TaxaTranslator_Results_wAttributes.csv)

[**Step 2: Return to the calculation tab and run the BCG
calculator**]{.underline}

The R code will perform the following steps:

1.  Mark non-distinct taxa (excluded from richness metrics)

2.  Calculate metric values for each sample

3.  Calculate BCG metric membership values for each sample

4.  Assign each sample membership in a BCG level

Note: the default setting is for the R code to mark
redundant/non-distinct taxa. If you want to use an alternate scheme,
uncheck the box, include your designations (TRUE/FALSE) in the input
file and name the column ‘EXCLUDE.’

[**Step 3: Download and unzip the results**]{.underline}

The files will be added to the appropriate subfolder (depending on the
community.

This brief memo
<a href="https://github.com/Blocktt/LowerBoiseBCGCalc/blob/main/inst/apps/LowerBoiseBCGCalc/www/links/FuzzySetExplanation_20260526.pdf" target="_blank">[PDF]</a>
provides background information on how the BCG model works.

**List of BCG calculation outputs.**

```{r table_outputs}
# Packages
library(readxl)
library(knitr)
library(kableExtra)

# Data
fn <- "OutputFileSubtabs.xlsx"
path <- file.path("files", fn)
df <- read_excel(path, sheet = "Calc_BCG")

options(knitr.kable.NA = '')
df %>%
  kable(escape = FALSE, format = "html") %>%
  kable_styling(full_width = F, position = "left")
```

**There are two additional outputs for the fish only.**

```{r table_fishoutputs}
# Packages
library(readxl)
library(knitr)
library(kableExtra)

# Data
fn <- "OutputFileSubtabs.xlsx"
path <- file.path("files", fn)
df <- read_excel(path, sheet = "Calc_BCG_Fish")

options(knitr.kable.NA = '')
df %>%
  kable(escape = FALSE, format = "html") %>%
  kable_styling(full_width = F, position = "left")
```

for each individual output file.
